question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution:
The correct answer is '**gnawed**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given passage is a story of a lion.
 
• The most appropriate word for the given blank is '**gnawed**'.
 
• It means 'to bite a bone, etc. many times with your back teeth'. (पिछले दाँतों से हड्‌डी आदि को अनेक बार काटना या कड़ी वस्‍तु को कुतरना)
 
 
• *Example: Fear of the future **gnawed** away at her all the time.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**Correct Passage:__** *One day, a few hunters came into the forest and took the lion with them. They tied him up against a tree. The lion was struggling to get away and started to whimper. Soon, a mouse walked past and noticed the lion in trouble. He quickly ran and **gnawed** on the ropes to set the lion free. Both of them then (5) ______ into the jungle.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• Let's look into the meaning of the other words given in the options:
 
 
• **Chew: To crush food into smaller, softer pieces with the teeth so that it can be swallowed.**

 
 
• ***Example:** This meat is difficult to **chew**.*
 
 
 
• **Nibble: To eat something by taking a lot of small bites.**
 
 
• ***Example:** A mouse has **nibbled **through the computer cables.*
 
 
 
• **Bitten: Use the teeth to cut into or through something.**
 
 
• ***Example:** He had nearly **bitten** his swollen tongue in two falling over an unseen peat.*
